Coverage, survival & limitations

Availability depends on the particular repository, locality, date range and record series. We have not established complete coverage for this collection. Follow each provider link for its holdings and access terms; a missing result is not proof of absence.

Reading the evidence: an index, transcript, provider search page and original image are different sources. A recorded image link does not mean its reading or identity match is confirmed. Inspect the assessment and source page before changing a family relationship. Repository guides checked 4 October 2026.

Reviewed newspaper notices

151 distinct notices from 205 retained pages, earliest first. Reprints of the same notice are merged; 205 pages have saved inline excerpts. Open a notice for its clipping, reading and profile assessment.

How to read these notices

Cards lead with the person named in the notice; profile candidates are assessed separately. Birth cutoffs labelled “by c.” are estimates, usually assuming an adult professional was at least 18; open the birth note for the basis. Event groups are broad navigation aids built from each notice’s record type. A relationship filter identifies family wording in the notice, not a proved match to a WikiTree family.

Mrs. Glasco

Christ-church-lane (husband’s watchmaking address)Birth unknown

Death reported; identified as the wife of Philip Glasco, junior, watchmaker.

Spouse / marriageDeath

Published 1765-09-28 · The Public Register, or, Freeman's Journal · p. 3

What the notice says

The death column reports Mrs. Glasco, wife of Mr. Philip Glasco, junior, watchmaker, in Christ-church-lane. Her given and maiden names are not printed.

Evidence and identity limits

The same junior designation, trade and Dublin lane make Glasgow-3932 a probable match to the younger Philip who married Teresa Plunkett in 1768. If the identification is correct, this records an earlier unnamed wife; do not identify her as Teresa or infer parents. The issue supplies a latest date for her death, not an exact day. Identity review (6 October 2026): Freeman's Journal death column (issue of 28 Sep 1765) for Mrs. Glasco, wife of Mr. Philip Glasco junior, watchmaker, Christ-church-lane, Dublin. Philip junior is the younger Dublin watchmaker, who already exists twice on WikiTree: Glasco-147 (the better-connected profile, with wives Braccan-2 and Plunkett-2805) and the project-created duplicate Glasgow-3932, whose live biography has been overwritten with an unrelated 1827 Kilrea Robert Glasgow text. The deceased wife is already modelled as Braccan-2. No new relationship is needed; the action is a merge and data clean-up.

[b. c. 1740; d. ?] · husband of the deceased
Why this candidate?

The notice's exact designation 'Philip Glasco, jun.', the watchmaking trade and Christ-church-lane agree with the 1768 marriage of 'Phil. Glasco the younger', watchmaker of Christ-church-lane, and with the 1772 Prerogative intestacy index entry 'Philip Glasco, the younger, Dublin, watchmaker' that Glasco-147 is built on (cited on Mangan-824 and Glasco-147). Only one younger Philip Glasco watchmaker existed in Dublin. Glasco-147 (b. c.1740, son of Glasco-146, spouses Braccan-2 and Plunkett-2805, children Glasco-149/150/169/174) and Glasgow-3932 (Phillip, b. before 1750, Co. [b. before 1747; d. c. 1765] · deceased wife of Philip Glasco junior
Why this candidate?

Braccan-2 ('Mary Braccan / Glasco', b. before 1747, d. 1765, spouse of Glasco-147) is the WikiTree profile created for this woman. Her only cited source is the Faulkner's Dublin Journal transcription of this same death. The notice identifies her only as the wife of Philip Glasco junior, so matching her to this profile is secure as a role match. However, the given name and maiden name on the profile are not supported. The RC baptism of Phil Glascoe at SS Michael & John, Dublin, in 1762 (DU-RC-BA-46402, quoted on Braccan-1) names the father Phil Glascoe and the mother only as 'Mary [nr]', and lists Mary Braccan as SPONSOR 2. Phil. Glasco the younger

Christ-church-lane, DublinBirth unknown

Marriage column identifies him as a watchmaker.

Teresa Plunkett

Church-street, DublinBirth unknown

Named as his bride in the marriage notice.

Spouse / marriageOccupation / trade

Published 1768-09-20 · The Public Register, or, Freeman's Journal · p. 3

What the notice says

The marriage column names Mr. Phil. Glasco the younger, of Christ-church-lane, watchmaker, and Miss Teresa Plunkett of Church-street.

Evidence and identity limits

The rare name, younger designation, trade, address and bride agree with the existing Philip junior evidence draft and compatible profile Glasgow-3932. This original corroborates the marriage reported in the Public Gazetteer extraction dated 17 September 1768; it does not itself supply that exact wedding date or prove his father. Keep him separate from the elder Philip and the later surname-only watchmaker. OCR Glafco represents printed Glasco. Identity review (6 October 2026): Freeman's Journal 20 Sep 1768 marriage of Mr. Phil. Glasco the younger, watchmaker of Christ-church-lane, to Miss Teresa Plunkett of Church-street. Both people already exist and are already linked as spouses on WikiTree: Glasco-147 and Plunkett-2805. Glasgow-3932 is a duplicate of the groom.

Who this may be

Phillip Glasco (Glasco-147)strong
[b. c. 1740; d. ?] · groom
Why this candidate?

The rare name, 'the younger', the watchmaking trade, Christ-church-lane and the bride all agree. Glasco-147 is already married on WikiTree to Plunkett-2805 (Teresa Plunkett), whose biography cites the 1768 Public Gazetteer extraction of this marriage. Glasco-147 is defined by the 1772 intestacy of 'Philip Glasco, the younger, Dublin, watchmaker'. Glasgow-3932 is the same man (duplicate, no spouse, biography now overwritten with an unrelated Kilrea text). See group 1050029120.

Plunkett-2805 (Plunkett-2805)strong
· bride
Why this candidate?

Plunkett-2805 (Teresa Plunkett / Glasco, b. before 1750, Co. Dublin, d. after 1771, spouse Glasco-147, child Glasco-174) was created from this marriage. Her biography quotes the Public Gazetteer: 'Mr. Philip Glasco Jnr of Christchurch-yard, Watchmaker, to the agreeable Miss Teresa Plunkett of Church-street'. The name, the street and the groom all agree, and no other Teresa Plunkett of the period exists on WikiTree (Plunkett-829, b. 1765 Westmeath, is too young and from a different place).

Michael Rogers

Place not statedBirth unknown

ordered to pay ten guineas after assaulting the Reverend Manasses Glasco

Occupation / trade

Published 1780-12-12 · The Public Register, or, Freeman's Journal · p. 6

What the notice says

Michael Rogers, for assaulting the Rev. Manasses Glasco, ordered to pay ten guineas, to be distributed in public charities by the prosecutor.

Evidence and identity limits

The original directly supports the clerical title Rev. for Manasses Glasco in 1780. Glasco-170 is a probable match to the Monkstown family account; his recorded birth BEFORE 1766 is a boundary, not a 1766 birth. The notice names no relatives or parish appointment. No relationship is upgraded. Identity review (6 October 2026): Freeman's Journal 12 Dec 1780 court report: Michael Rogers was fined ten guineas for assaulting the Rev. Manasses Glasco. The only Manasses Glasco or Glasgow on WikiTree is Glasco-170 (Rev. Manasses, said to be assistant curate of Monkstown, died before his widow Susanna remarried in June 1784), and the identity is now graded strong. The notice names no kin.

Who this may be

Manasses Glasco (Glasco-170)probable
[b. before 1766; d. before 1784] · assault victim (clergyman)
Why this candidate?

The full name is unique in the surname study and the clerical title fits: duplicate searches for Manasses Glasco, Manasses Glasgow and Manasseh Glasgow return only Glasco-170. The YouWho Dowling family account calls Manasses Glasco assistant curate of Monkstown and says his widow Susanna married Dionysius Dowling at Monkstown in June 1784. The profile also cites M. Wade Mahon's note of a 'Rev. Mr Glasco' who was first assistant at a Blackrock school and advertised for boarders in 1782. A Rev. Manasses Glasco in Dublin in Dec 1780 fits all of this, and no rival Manasses exists. The match is strong for the person; it does not validate the profile's other claims. Two caveats.
